turns.asr_text: Walk me through how a hash map works.

turns.text_generated:
Alright, let’s break it down in a fun and simple way! Imagine a hash map is like a giant set of mailboxes. Each mailbox has its own unique number, called a hash. When you want to store something, you run it through a special function, a hash function, that quickly figures out which mailbox it belongs to. Then it pops your data right in there.

…and voilà! The hash function tells you exactly which mailbox to check. You open it up and—boom—there’s your data, fast and efficient. Now, sometimes two different keys might lead to the same mailbox—this is called a collision. Good hash maps handle collisions by storing both items in that mailbox, maybe as a little list inside. When you look up your data, it quickly scans that list to find the exact match. 

So, in a nutshell, a hash map is just a super speedy way to store and retrieve data by using these hash functions and mailboxes.
